findings.where: The blue 'Get Mark's briefings on PPP reform' band with its Subscribe button, directly under the hero (on desktop it starts at the fold; on phone it sits right under the email action, within the first scroll)
findings.fault: A second call to action competes with the one personal action. It also offers a briefings service that doesn't exist: Subscribe only jumps to #subscribe, and the page has no sign-up there. It switches to the third person ('Mark's'), so it reads like a firm's marketing banner rather than Mark speaking.
findings.who_objects: The founder, whose brief sets one message and one action and says the copy must never invent claims; it must also not read as salesy. A development-bank visitor who presses Subscribe gets nothing back, and a promise that leads nowhere costs Mark credibility before anyone has written to him.

findings.where: Hero and header: the lede under the heading, and the bar holding only the name and logo with no navigation
findings.fault: Nothing above the fold or anywhere on the page shows evidence of Mark's work. There are no regions or countries, no named bodies that asked him, no roles or dates. The hero photo is at an event, but the caption doesn't name it. The header has no nav, so there is no route to a CV, a list of work or an About page. The lede says whom he advises but not where or on what work.
findings.who_objects: Staff at a multilateral development bank who choose individual advisors against terms of reference. Before writing, they need to see that he has done this kind of work for bodies like theirs in their region (first-visit trust items 2, 3, 6 and 14, and 'Feel the CV'). A first-person opinion line is not enough to justify an email.

findings.where: The lecture card at the end of the article specimen ('Streamlining the PPP Process … Lecture · 23 April 2026')
findings.fault: The newest talk is shown with its date but not its venue or host. The card says nothing about who invited Mark to speak, which is the part that shows his standing.
findings.who_objects: A procurement reader who judges standing by who asked: the venue is the checkable fact that turns a PDF into proof ('Feel the CV': the newest article or talk with its venue).
